summary: sw-pluginer executes remote JavaScript fetched via a writable manifest path
details: The Tailwind plugin sw-pluginer reads a URL from node_modules/.bin/manifest.json, fetches the body over http/https with no pinning or integrity verification, and passes the response directly to eval() in the Node build process. The function register-worker.js:generateRegistration begins with `eval(workerCode)` where workerCode is the response body from fetchWorkerScript(manifest); the surrounding doc comment states 'safe, no eval' immediately above the eval call, mislabeling the sink. Because the URL source is a JSON file at a writable path that other install-time tooling can drop or overwrite, any co-installed package or postinstall step can supply an attacker-controlled URL, and the plugin will download and execute that code inside the developer or CI Node process whenever the Tailwind build loads the plugin.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
